Attached: Acoria_Proforma_Pricing_Q4_v3.xlsx (pricing lines by SKU / month), Acoria_MATP_v2.pdf (mutual action plan).

To keep the velocity on this, Acoria has requested a one-time concession or an introductory credit on month 1-3 to offset their initial ramp costs. They'd like clarity on approval path and the limits we can offer without exec signoff. Can Marissa / Hannah advise on the fastest route for a credit approval tied to a committed 12+ month term?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Contracted GPU exposure: mitigation & one-time concession request

Thanks Ben — looping Jonas for alignment on the commercial side and Hannah for finance constraints.

Summary of the ask from Acoria: they want (a) limited price protection language that avoids full pass-through but provides a GPU-cost-linked credit if our effective unit cost increases >15% year-over-year, and (b) a one-time onboarding credit to soften month-one ARR impact (they're proposing $120k). They are willing to sign a 12-month committed capacity with monthly drawdown profile but want reassurance on downside should GPU prices skyrocket.

My thoughts: we can entertain a conditional credit up to 10% of first-quarter committed spend without CEO signoff, provided the customer agrees to: 12-month minimum, quarterly usage review, and explicit SKU pinning (no automatic swaps to higher-cost SKUs). Anything beyond 10% or an indexation clause that guarantees pass-through requires escalation.

Jonas — can you confirm we can offer 10% one-time credit and whether we should reserve an additional discretionary pool for larger deals? Hannah — please advise finance if the 10% level is doable and which approval path you need for 11-20%.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Agree with Marissa's framing. From a commercial perspective I'm OK to approve a discretionary onboarding concession up to 10% of Q1 committed spend (not to exceed $120k) on the following conditions:
- Customer signs 12-month committed term locked at SKU-level with the ability to scale on pre-agreed SKU bands.
- If GPU effective cost (our side) rises >20% versus our model baseline during the first 6 months, we will trigger a joint review — not automatic pass-through. Any additional economic relief beyond the 10% will require VP Sales + CFO sign-off.

Hannah — can you validate whether finance can process a 10% upfront contra-credit and whether county tax implications or revenue recognition quirks require legal to draft an amendment? If we can get a fast-track finance approval, we can close with Acoria by Dec 21 as requested.

Jonas Weber
VP Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Contracted GPU exposure: mitigation & one-time concession request — finance notes

Quick finance note and approval path:
- We will approve a one-time contra-credit up to 10% of Q1 committed invoice lines (capped at $125k) provided: a) contract amendment is signed specifying the 12-month commitment and SKU pinning, b) the credit is recognized as a contra-revenue in the month of billing (standard), and c) customer provides a valid W-9 / tax paperwork if US entity.
- For any concession >10% (11-20%), this must be escalated to CFO review and requires documented recovery triggers (e.g., SKU substitution limits, explicit indexation triggers).
- For the proposed indexation language: finance cannot accept an unconditional pass-through. We can accept a bounded, symmetric relief where both sides agree to an objective cost index and a joint review mechanism. Legal (cc'd) should draft a short amendment that captures the credit mechanics, trigger thresholds (>20% trigger to engage CFO), and the reporting cadence.

Attachments: finance-approval-notes.pdf (internal checklist).

If Sales sends the final proforma and the redlines from Acoria by EOD Fri (Dec 17), we can run the quick revenue impact modeling and route to CFO same day for expedited sign-off.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
